newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares end higher, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares end higher, off highs.

text.p: Turkish stocks gained 1.02 percent on Friday in selective activity led by financial sector shares.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 brushed a high of 1,987 in the afternoon session, ending 1.02 percent or 20 points higher at 1,973
Trade volume fell 19.1 percent to 26.6 trillion lira ($165 million) from Thursday's 32.9 trillion lira ($204 million).
Brokers said demand for Eregli and other state shares eased. Demand was high on Friday for private sector blue chips and banks, brokers said.
"There was selective demand mostly in shares with expectations for high profit. Banks were also traded heavily on profit expectations," said Ayse Celik from Tekstil Securities.
The index rose 4.45 percent this week after a six percent loss a week ago.

Of the 249 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 131 to 65 and 53 were stable. The IMKB Industrial barely up 0.05 percent to 1,904, the IMKB Services inched up 0.46 percent to 1,932 and the IMKB Financial gained 2.81 percent to 2,123.
The highest rise was seen in the index representing the banking sector with 4.10 percent gain.

Leading active share of the session was flat steel producer Eregli, down 1,250 lira to 25,500 after a sharp 20 percent rise of last two days. Eregli was followed by electronics utility Vestel up 600 lira to 11,000 and Is Bank C Series ISCTR, up 2,000 to 55,000.
The three made up 19.4 percent of the total volume.
